FORM.AppraisalReportContentName: Market Conditions Addendum to the Appraisal Report

MARKET.SalesConcessionDescription: There have been no substantial increase or decrease in seller concessions trends in the past twelve months. Concessions for new and existing homes are apparent in the market generally tied to higher priced units and new builder inventory. Incentives range from 3 to 5% of the price and can include upgrade packages, HOA fees, etc. depending on the specific subdivision or sellers need to close the deal. Existing homes competitive to the subject had few if any concessions associated with the deal, unless the property was significantly over priced or vacant new home inventory.
MARKET.NeighborhoodMarketabilityFactorsDescript: In the past three months there has been no substantial increase in REO sales and foreclosure and they do not appear to have negatively affected listing or sales trends in the area. Foreclosure activity stable and is concentrated in homes purchased at or near the market peak in the mid 2008 period. Homes in the immediate area of the subject do not fall in that general parameter and prices have since stabilized within the past 36 months.
MARKET.DataSourceDescription: All market data above has been derived from MLS data, tax record data, and realtor input information and all information is considered reliable.
MARKET.MarketTrendsReconciliationComment: The purpose of this addendum is to provide the lender/client with a clear and accurate understanding of the market trends and conditions prevalent in the subject neighborhood. This is a required addendum for all appraisal reports with an effective date of April 1, 2009 or later. The overall trends appear to be stable, and supply and demand appear to be in balance.

VALUATION_METHODS._AdditionalDescription:
This inspection takes place post recent severe storm declared by FEMA, and the subject has not been affected by these storms. The subject property is free from damage and the disaster has had no affect on value or marketability.
Due to the subject's size and location the subject's appraised value is lower than the predominant values in the municipality. This does not represent an under improvement and does not appear to negatively affect marketability or marketing time.
All utilities were on and operational at the time of inspection. No warranties are implied by this statement and a home inspection to verify their functionality by a licensed home inspector is recommended.
The current use of the subject as a residential property is the most financially feasible, physically possible, and legal use of the of the improved property. The subject's current use is therefore its highest and best use as per USPAP.
Reasonable exposure time for properties in this area is between 0-90 days.
The appraisal was prepared in accordance with the requirements of Title XI of the FIRREA of 1989, as amended (12 U.S.C. 3331 et seq.), and any implementing regulations.
The Square Footage-Method for Calculating: ANSI Z765-2021 - was used for measuring, calculating and reporting the gross living and non-gross living areas of the subject property. All measurement were calculated to the nearest inch or 1/10th of a foot.
Due to the limited number of comparables in the subject's neighborhood the appraiser was unable to bracket the subject's GLA with a comparable sale or listing. This was unavoidable and has no negative impact on the appraisers final opinion of value or the marketability of the subject property.Bracketing is not a part of appraising, it is a lender guideline. This appraiser will attempt to bracket comparables when possible, but when the market area does not provide comparables that can be bracketed, this appraiser will utilize the best comparables available that are similar to the subject and support the estimated market value of the subject's real property.
Due to the unique location, features and size of the subject property, in combination with the limited number of available comparables the appraiser was forced to exceed 10% line, 15% net, and 25% gross adjustment guidelines for several of the comparables. This was unavoidable and has no negative impact on the appraisers final opinion of value.
Due to the limited number of comparables in the subject's neighborhood the appraiser was forced to utilize sales in which there were wide variations between the adjusted and unadjusted prices and the subject's final opinion of value. This was unavoidable and has no negative impact on the appraisers final opinion of value or the marketability of the subject property.
Smoke and CO detectors which are required by local/state code were present and appeared functional at the time of the appraiser's field inspection. Water heater straps are not required by state or local code.

COST_ANALYSIS.SiteEstimatedValueComment: Site value was derived via the extraction method, and local land sales when available.
COST_ANALYSIS._Comment: Based upon an age life of 60 years the remaining economic life is 32 years. Due to the lack of buildable land the land to building ratios typically exceed 30%.

SALES_COMPARISON._Comment: GLA was adjusted by $55.00 a square foot, and all other adjustments were derived via market reaction and paired sales where available. Due to the lack of comparables in the area the appraiser was forced to use sales which exceeded 6 months in age, and over one mile in distance from the subject property. All sales cited were the best available at the time of inspection. The median sales to list price ratio is about 100% if priced fairly. There are typically no sellers concessions present in the subject market area though they are not unusual. There are currently 2+/- active comparable listings in the area this quarter. Comparables five and six are active and pending listings which were included to demonstrate the ongoing stability of the market and the current marketability of comparable homes in the subject's neighborhood.

INCOME_ANALYSIS._Comment: Estimated market rents are based on size, utility, condition and location of the individual units. All comparables used were considered to be the best available at the time of inspection.

MULTIFAMILY_RENT_SCHEDULE.RentalDataAnalysisComment: All rental information was obtained via the owner, local realtors and the MLS and is deemed reliable.
MULTIFAMILY_RENT_SCHEDULE.MarketRentalDataComment: Actual and estimated rents coincide. Typically, tenants pay all utilities except water and sewer.

MULTIFAMILY_RENTALS.RentalDataAnalysisComment: Estimated market rents are based on size, utility, condition and location of the individual units. All comparables used were considered to be the best available at the time of inspection.

_RECONCILIATION._SummaryComment: Most weight in the sales comparison approach was placed on comparables one and three which were most similar to the subject property in location and condition/quality of construction respectively. Secondary emphasis was placed on comparables two and four which were utilized to bracket the features and amenities of the subject property where possible.
